_comment: Canonical head-tracking config schema, shared by the C# and C++ halves of the
library. scripts/generate-config-schema.mjs turns this into
csharp/src/CameraUnlock.Core/Config/ConfigKeySchema.g.cs and
cpp/include/cameraunlock/config/config_key_schema.g.h; `pixi run check-config-schema`
fails when either generated file is stale, which is what stops the two languages
drifting apart the way the fleet's hand-rolled key spellings did.
Matching is SECTION-LESS and case-insensitive: a key is lowercased and stripped of
'_' and '-' before lookup, so Network.UDPPort, udp_port and Udp-Port all resolve to
the same concept. `section` and `key` below therefore describe the FILE LAYOUT and
the documentation, not the parse. Every spelling under `aliases` keeps working, so
adding a canonical name never breaks an existing user's config.
Adding a concept or an alias is safe. Removing one, or moving an alias between
concepts, is a breaking change for every config file already on a user's disk.
`canonical` says whether the canonical config format writes the concept. One with
`canonical: false` keeps its aliases and its flat-reader parsing, and its
`canonical_reason` is the one line a player is shown for such a key in a canonical file.
Every canonical concept has a `file_comment`, the one or two lines written above its key
for players (`doc` is the developer text), and may have a `range` (`min`, `max`, either
optional; a value outside it is invalid, never clamped), a `codec` ('hotkey' on the key
lists) and a `canonical_default`, the binding list a canonical file starts with. The
`default` and the field initialisers of a key the flat readers read keep the single key
name those readers have always shipped, because changing a default is a breaking change.
A hotkey concept no flat reader reads has its `canonical_default` as its `default`.
`non_canonical_keys` names settings no canonical file carries that are not concepts: the
tracker owns pose shaping, and deadzones, response curves and unit scales were never schema
concepts. Their spellings are not aliases, so neither flat reader resolves them and nothing
binds them to a field. A group's `sections` are sections that hold only such settings: any
key in one is the group's, whatever it is spelled. A canonical table refuses a game-local
row named by a spelling or in such a section, applying a canonical file reports either as
NonCanonicalConcept with the group's `canonical_reason`, and the canonical config lint fails
a file holding one.

deliberately_unaliased.reason: AMBIGUOUS UNDER SECTION-LESS MATCHING. Mods ship these under [Sensitivity] meaning a sensitivity multiplier and under [Deadzone] meaning degrees of deadzone, and the nine repos non_canonical_keys Deadzone names read both sections from one file. Normalisation throws the section away, so aliasing the bare names onto either concept would read one of them as the other. Neither is a setting any more: the Sensitivity and Deadzone groups of non_canonical_keys list those two sections, so a key in either draws the group's reason whatever it is spelled.
4 repos use [Hotkeys] Position for the position toggle key, but the bare word is too generic to claim section-lessly. PositionToggleKey, TogglePositionKey and PositionKey are aliased instead.

Bare nouns whose meaning comes entirely from their section. Enabled and Enable were briefly excepted and aliased onto EnableOnStartup, on the grounds that the 39 repos writing [Position] Enabled spell the concept PositionEnabled in code. They do in code; they do not in the FILE, which is what this table reads. Matching is section-less, so a file carrying [Position] Enabled=false resolved it to EnableOnStartup and turned the whole mod off with position tracking left on, silently. [Flashlight] Enabled did the same. Unaliased, that line now resolves to nothing and is ignored, which leaves the master switch on its default - the safe direction, and a mod that wants the [General] key read has EnableOnStartup, AutoEnable, StartEnabled and three more spellings to name it by. Multiplier is the same shape and is shipped today by still-wakes-the-deep ([Torch] Multiplier) and resident-evil-requiem ([Flashlight] Multiplier): section-less, it is as generic as Scale, so those two read their own key rather than the schema resolving it to LightMultiplier for them.

4 repos smooth position independently of rotation. This schema deliberately shares one smoothing pair between the two, so there is nothing to bind PositionSmoothing to. Adding a separate position smoothing pair is a schema change, not an alias.

Chord modifiers, not key names. A different concept from the *Key entries. A canonical file has no Chord* key at all: a chord is an ordinary item of its action's key list (ToggleKey=End, Ctrl+Shift+Y), and a game's legacy import folds a chord switch or letter row into that list. The canonical config lint refuses any key whose name starts with Chord.

Real cross-repo concepts with no field in HeadTrackingConfigData or its C++ twin to bind to. Aliasing a key onto nothing would advertise a setting that does not work. Each needs a concept and a field before it gets an alias.

default_conflicts.note: The schema default is true. A source and INI sweep of the fleet on 2026-09-23 found three repos that start in camera-local yaw: sonic-racing-crossworlds ([Tracking] WorldSpaceYaw, false in code and in the shipped INI, which calls camera-local the recommendation for the game's loops and walls), pixeljunk-monsters-2 (BepInEx [Rotation] WorldSpaceYaw bound with default false, described as suiting the tilted top-down camera) and battlefield-bad-company-2 (no config key at all; it starts camera-local and only the yaw-mode hotkey changes it). dying-light-2 and dishonored-2 ([Rotation] WorldLockedYaw) defaulted false until their commits 0307ede and 8184371 moved the compiled default, the shipped INI and the launcher seed to true; a HeadTracking.ini already on a user's disk keeps the value it names. quake-ii-rtx and sleeping-dogs, once listed here, default true in code and INI. WorldLockedYaw is aliased because it is genuinely the same concept with the same polarity, but a mod that adopts this schema's DEFAULT in place of its own flips behaviour for its existing users. Check the mod's own default before wiring the table in.

concepts.doc: Smoothing applied when the tracker runs on this machine. 0-1.
file_comment: Smoothing when the tracker runs on this PC. 0 is the least, 1 the most.

concepts.doc: Smoothing applied when the tracker is a device on the network. 0-1.
file_comment: Smoothing when the tracker is another device on the network, such as a phone.
0 is the least, 1 the most.

concepts.doc: true rotates yaw around world up (horizon locked); false around the camera's own up.
file_comment: true: yaw turns around the world's up axis. false: around the camera's own up axis.

concepts.doc: Keep the aim direction on the mouse rather than on the head.
file_comment: true: your aim stays with the mouse or controller while your head moves the view.

concepts.doc: Draw the decoupled aim reticle.
concepts.canonical_reason: Whether a reticle is shown is not a setting.

concepts.doc: Reticle RGBA as four 0-1 floats, comma separated.
concepts.canonical_reason: The reticle colour is not a setting.

concepts.doc: Whether rotational (yaw, pitch, roll) tracking is applied. Together with PositionEnabled it records the tracking mode. There is no alias: no config in the fleet named a rotation switch when this key was added, and a bare Enabled stays unmatched; see deliberately_unaliased.
file_comment: true: turning your head turns the view.
Tracking mode at startup, with PositionEnabled. The mode hotkey changes both.

concepts.doc: How long, in milliseconds, the newest tracker packet counts as current. The mods that read it compare the age of the last packet with it every frame and stop following the tracker once the packet is older: most hold the last pose (bioshock-infinite, dead-space, dying-light, outlast), mirrors-edge hands the camera back to the game. 500 is the fixed liveness window of core's UdpReceiver (kConnectionTimeoutMs), which is where the fleet's default came from. A window of 0 or less never counts a packet as current, so tracking never applies: refused below 1. No aliases: every fleet reader spells it DataFreshnessMs, under [General] in all but stormworks ([Advanced]) and fusion-360 ([Tracking]), and beamng keeps dataFreshnessMs in JSON.
file_comment: Milliseconds a tracker packet stays current. Once the tracker has sent nothing
for this long, the mod stops following it until data arrives again.

concepts.doc: Whether positional (6DOF) tracking is applied.
file_comment: true: moving your head moves the view.
Tracking mode at startup, with RotationEnabled. The mode hotkey changes both.

concepts.doc: false means the game never applies positional tracking and the tracking-mode control skips the position modes, so head tracking runs rotation only whatever RotationEnabled and PositionEnabled say. For a game where position cannot work. One spelling fleet-wide: a game-local key may not reuse a concept name, so only a concept keeps every game on this one. No aliases: no config in the fleet named the switch when it was added. Core only parses it.
file_comment: false: head tracking runs rotation only, whatever RotationEnabled and PositionEnabled say,
and the mode hotkey skips the modes that use position.

concepts.doc: The lean while aiming down sights, in a shooter with an aim state and positional tracking (the shooter-ads-handling skill). false is sights locked: the lean never takes the eye off the sight line, because the mod draws the weapon from the clean eye or eases the lean out through AdsFade while aiming. true is true free look: the lean stays in full, the weapon stays put in the world and the head moves around it. A persisted preference: the TrueFreeLookKey toggle saves it, so a mod marks the row Writable. A mod without positional tracking has one mode and binds neither concept. It sits under [Position] because the lean is all it changes and it exists only where positional tracking does, and a key goes in the schema section of its subject (docs/canonical-config.md), as CollisionEnabled does. No aliases: true_free_look is read only by a game's legacy import. Section-less matching resolves that spelling to this concept, so a canonical file that holds it draws MisplacedKey and is not read. The deprecated flat readers (HeadTrackingConfigData.ApplyValues, HeadTrackingConfig::ApplyValues) do not read this concept.
file_comment: false: while you aim down the sights, leaning keeps your eye on the sights.
true: the weapon stays put and your head moves freely around it (true free look).

concepts.doc: Lateral position sensitivity multiplier.
concepts.canonical_reason: The mod applies the head pose as the tracker sends it, with no sensitivity of its own.

concepts.doc: Vertical position sensitivity multiplier.
concepts.canonical_reason: The mod applies the head pose as the tracker sends it, with no sensitivity of its own.

concepts.doc: Depth position sensitivity multiplier.
concepts.canonical_reason: The mod applies the head pose as the tracker sends it, with no sensitivity of its own.

concepts.doc: Maximum lateral displacement in metres, applied symmetrically.
file_comment: How far, in metres, leaning left or right can move the view.

concepts.doc: Maximum UPWARD displacement in metres.
file_comment: How far, in metres, raising your head can move the view.

concepts.doc: Maximum DOWNWARD displacement in metres. Usually tighter than the upward limit so the camera does not clip into the player body. When a file names PositionLimitY and NOT this key, the up limit is mirrored into it: one vertical limit in the file means one vertical limit in the clamp. Leaving the down side at its default is what caps a raised LimitY at 0.20m downward.
file_comment: How far, in metres, lowering your head can move the view.

concepts.doc: Maximum FORWARD displacement in metres. Negative z is forward, so this is the lower bound of the z clamp.
file_comment: How far, in metres, leaning forward can move the view.

concepts.doc: Maximum BACKWARD displacement in metres, the upper bound of the z clamp.
file_comment: How far, in metres, leaning back can move the view.

concepts.doc: Sweep the level between the clean eye and the lean target and cut the lean to what the room leaves. Ships off in a mod whose trace has not been confirmed in game, because an unverified channel either blocks on nothing or blocks on everything; a mod turns it on once its log shows the sweep engaging on real geometry. Mods spell the section differently - amnesia-rebirth carries it under [Camera] - and core's alias matching is section-less, so the section here is a readability choice.
file_comment: true: leaning stops at walls instead of moving the view through them.

concepts.doc: How far off a blocking surface the eye is held, in the engine's own units. It must EXCEED the camera's near clip distance or geometry is culled before the eye reaches it and the wall goes transparent anyway. CollisionRadius is the spelling where the standoff IS a sweep radius; CollisionMargin where the query is a line and the standoff lives in the clamp.
file_comment: How far the view is held off a wall when you lean into it, in the game's own units.

concepts.doc: Which trace channel the sweep runs on, for engines whose query needs one. Which channel a level's geometry blocks is a project setting rather than an engine constant, so it is a value to try and read back out of the log. Omitted by mods whose cast takes no channel.
file_comment: Which of the game's collision channels the wall check tests against.

concepts.doc: How quickly the lean reopens once an obstruction clears, on the same 0-1 scale as every other smoothing value in the fleet. 0.9 is a 200ms time constant. Tightening is never smoothed: easing INTO a smaller allowance leaves the eye inside the geometry for the length of the ease, which is the whole bug.
file_comment: How gently the view eases back out after a wall stopped a lean.
0 is the quickest, 1 the slowest.

concepts.doc: Invert the lateral position axis.
concepts.canonical_reason: The mod applies the head pose as the tracker sends it, with no axis inversion of its own.

concepts.doc: Invert the vertical position axis.
concepts.canonical_reason: The mod applies the head pose as the tracker sends it, with no axis inversion of its own.

concepts.doc: Invert the depth position axis. An engine whose camera-local +z is forward negates at the boundary instead of setting this.
concepts.canonical_reason: The mod applies the head pose as the tracker sends it, with no axis inversion of its own.

concepts.doc: Metres from the neck pivot forward to the point the tracker watches. 0 disables pivot compensation.
file_comment: Metres from the pivot of your neck forward to the point the tracker follows.
Used to remove the lean that turning your head adds. 0 here and in TrackerPivotUp turns it off.

concepts.doc: Metres from the neck pivot up to the point the tracker watches.
file_comment: Metres from the pivot of your neck up to the point the tracker follows.

concepts.doc: Key that toggles head tracking on and off.
file_comment: Turns head tracking on and off.

concepts.doc: Key that toggles positional (6DOF) tracking on and off.
concepts.canonical_reason: CycleTrackingModeKey is the hotkey that switches positional tracking.

concepts.doc: Key that toggles the decoupled aim reticle.
concepts.canonical_reason: The reticle has no toggle key.

concepts.doc: Key that cycles the tracking mode. Empty leaves it unbound.
file_comment: Changes the tracking mode: rotation and position, rotation only, position only.

concepts.doc: Key that toggles world-locked versus camera-local yaw.
file_comment: Switches yaw between the world's up axis and the camera's own (WorldSpaceYaw).

concepts.doc: Key list that toggles TrueFreeLook, between sights locked and true free look. Only in a mod that binds TrueFreeLook. The deprecated flat readers do not read it, so nothing holds its default to a single key name: the default and the field initialisers are the canonical_default.
file_comment: Switches between keeping your eye on the sights and true free look (TrueFreeLook).

concepts.doc: Retained so existing callers keep parsing. No mod polls it: the tracker app owns the centre.
concepts.canonical_reason: The mod keeps no centre of its own: centre the view in your tracker app.

concepts.doc: Point a carried light where the head is looking rather than where the body is aiming. The two aliases are the spellings actually shipped - repo (FlashlightFollowsHead) and prey (CompensateFlashlight). The bare Enabled that still-wakes-the-deep and resident-evil-requiem ship under their own section stays unmatched on purpose, because section-less it is the master switch; see deliberately_unaliased.
file_comment: true: a light you carry points where you look instead of where you aim.

concepts.doc: How far the light turns relative to the head. 1.5 leads the view; 1.0 matches it; 0 pins the beam to the aim. A value outside [0, 5] is rejected with a log line and the previous one stands - not clamped. The two aliases are the spellings actually shipped: repo (FlashlightMultiplier) and prey (FlashlightScale). See cameraunlock::effects::kDefaultLightMultiplier for why it leads.
file_comment: How far the light turns for each degree your head turns.
1 matches the view, 0 keeps the light on your aim.

retired.doc: Retired and IGNORED. Replaced by LocalSmoothing and RemoteSmoothing. Not migrated: the old value carried a hidden 0.15 floor, so the number in an existing config does not mean what it used to.

non_canonical_keys.doc: Rotation and position multipliers that are no concept's alias. Fleet spellings on 2026-09-25: [tuning] rot_scale (dead-rising-2, mafia-ii-definitive-edition; sleeping-dogs names it as a retired key), which scales all three rotation axes; [ExtendedView] YawGain and PitchGain (assassins-creed-origins), which amplify the head angles fed to the game's Extended View; [General] PositionSensitivity (south-park-the-stick-of-truth), one multiplier on all three position axes. RollGain is the third of that set, and the bare Sensitivity, RotationSensitivity, RotationMultiplier, RotationGain, PositionMultiplier, PositionGain and LeanScale are the plain names a mod would give one; no fleet config file read them on 2026-09-25. The gates match these spellings and nothing else, so a sensitivity under a spelling no group lists passes them as a game-local row. The section is the schema's own [Sensitivity], listed so that a key in it no concept names (the bare Yaw, Pitch and Roll most mods wrote there) draws this group's reason too.
non_canonical_keys.canonical_reason: The mod applies the head pose as the tracker sends it, with no sensitivity of its own.

non_canonical_keys.doc: Per-axis signs a player can edit, which is user-facing inversion. [tuning] sign_yaw and the rest are dead-rising-2's and mafia-ii-definitive-edition's; mafia-ii ships sign_yaw and sign_roll at -1 to match its engine, which the conversion folds into the mod's axis code. The section is the schema's own [Inversion], listed for the same reason as [Sensitivity].
non_canonical_keys.canonical_reason: The mod applies the head pose as the tracker sends it, with no axis inversion of its own.

non_canonical_keys.doc: Deadzones are pose shaping, which the tracker owns. The spellings are the fleet's own on 2026-09-25: [Tracking] Deadzone (abzu, prey), [Rotation] Deadzone (quake-ii-rtx), [Smoothing] DeadzoneDeg (read by bully-scholarship-edition, burnout-paradise-the-ultimate-box, deus-ex-human-revolution, red-eclipse and south-park-the-stick-of-truth, and listed as a dead key by bioshock-infinite, outlast and spec-ops-the-line), [Tracking] DeadzoneYaw/Pitch/Roll (homeworld-remastered-collection; deadzone_yaw in minecraft-java-edition), [Rotation] YawDeadzone/PitchDeadzone/RollDeadzone (control-ultimate-edition, fusion-360), peak's Enable Deadzone in PascalCase, and DeadzoneMin/DeadzoneMax, the names core's own AxisConfig profile format writes. No fleet config reads a Deadband; those are the other plain name for one. The section [Deadzone] is where black-and-white, black-mesa, dorfromantik, fallout-new-vegas, half-life-2, portal, portal-2, subnautica and titanfall-2 read a bare Yaw, Pitch and Roll, so every key in it draws this group's reason.
non_canonical_keys.canonical_reason: The mod applies the head pose as the tracker sends it, with no deadzone of its own.

non_canonical_keys.doc: Response curves are pose shaping, which the tracker owns. SensitivityCurve and CurveStrength are the names core's own AxisConfig profile format writes (ProfileSerializer, as AxisMapping.<Axis>.SensitivityCurve). No fleet config file read a curve on 2026-09-25; the other spellings are the plain names a mod would give one.
non_canonical_keys.canonical_reason: The mod applies the head pose as the tracker sends it, with no response curve of its own.

non_canonical_keys.doc: Game units per metre of head movement. Converting the tracker's metres to the engine's units is the mod's boundary code, like its axis signs, not a setting: a player-edited scale is a position sensitivity under another name (homeworld-remastered-collection's PositionScale comment tells players to raise it for stronger parallax, black-and-white calls WorldScale its main tuning knob). Owner ruling 2026-09-25: the conversion folds the shipped value into the mod's code as a constant, and a value the player changed is dropped as PoseShaping and logged. Fleet spellings on 2026-09-25: PositionScale (read by dishonored, dishonored-definitive-edition, fusion-360, homeworld-remastered-collection, persona-5-royal, red-eclipse, spec-ops-the-line and thief, and named as a retired key by arkham-city, bioshock-infinite and outlast), PositionScaleUU (mirrors-edge), pos_scale (read by dead-rising-2 and mafia-ii-definitive-edition, named as a retired key by sleeping-dogs), WorldScale (black-and-white, black-mesa, half-life-2, portal, portal-2, titanfall-2), UnitsPerMeter (quake-ii-rtx) and world_units_per_metre (a-plague-tale-innocence). UnitsPerMetre and WorldUnitsPerMeter are those names with the other spelling of metre. metaphor-refantazio reads its scale as a bare [Position] Scale, which this group cannot list: matching is section-less, and spec-ops-the-line's [FieldOfView] Scale and rv-there-yet's [Reticle] Scale are the same spelling for settings that are not pose shaping. The lint refuses a bare Scale in any canonical file, but a canonical table accepts it as a game-local row and apply reports a stray one as an unknown key without this group's reason, so that conversion folds the scale into code and drops the legacy value by hand through LegacyPoseShaping.
non_canonical_keys.canonical_reason: The mod converts your head movement to the game's units itself, so the scale is not a setting.
